T: Quiet man. Loud appetite. Lots of milk.
D: A solitary hitman takes in a 12-year-old girl after her family is killed.
P: Pour a glass of milk every time Léon does.
S: Léon's French roots, simple and exact

Crusty baguette with thick cultured butter, shaved ham and cornichons, cut into bites the Paris café way. Warm 1 baguette at 200C for 5 minutes and cool slightly. Split lengthways and spread both sides generously with 80g soft cultured butter. Lay 200g thinly sliced leg ham inside, add 8 sliced cornichons and a little cracked pepper. Close, press firmly and cut into 12 pieces. Serve with Dijon on the side.
the plain lunch of a man who owns one plant and one chair
Mixed olives warmed in olive oil with orange peel, thyme and a crushed garlic clove, cornichons and pickled onions alongside.
the back room of Tony's restaurant in Little Italy

Torn bocconcini and sweet cherry tomatoes dressed in bright basil oil, flaky salt and black pepper, with grilled bread. Blitz 1 bunch basil leaves with 80ml olive oil and a pinch of salt until bright green. Tear 300g bocconcini and halve 250g cherry tomatoes. Arrange on a plate, spoon over the basil oil and finish with flaky salt and cracked pepper. Brush 8 slices ciabatta with oil, grill 2 minutes a side and serve alongside.
M: the French touch, for a man of very simple habits

Ham and Gruyère toasted sandwich spread with Dijon, topped with béchamel and more Gruyère, baked until golden and blistered. Melt 30g butter, stir in 30g plain flour for 1 minute, then whisk in 300ml milk and simmer 3 minutes. Add nutmeg, salt and 50g grated Gruyère. Spread 8 slices thick white bread with Dijon, fill 4 with 200g ham and 100g Gruyère and close. Top with the béchamel and 50g more Gruyère. Bake at 220C for 12 minutes, then grill for 2 minutes until blistered.
the restaurant back room where the jobs are handed out
Spaghetti pomodoro: garlic gently cooked in oil, San Marzano tomatoes crushed by hand, simmered 25 minutes, finished with basil and a knob of butter, parmesan.
W: his plant, which always gets the window
Layer chocolate mousse (melted dark chocolate folded into whipped cream and whipped egg whites) with crushed chocolate biscuit "soil" in small terracotta-style cups, a mint sprig planted on top.
K: Léon drinks milk, two litres at a time

Ice-cold milk blended thick with vanilla ice cream, malted milk powder and honey, poured into tall frosted glasses. Chill 4 tall glasses in the freezer for 15 minutes. Blend 600ml cold full cream milk, 6 scoops vanilla ice cream, 4 tbsp malted milk powder and 1 tbsp honey until thick and smooth. Pour into the frosted glasses and dust each with a little more malt powder.

m.note: the restaurant back room where the jobs are handed out
m.how: Gently cook 4 sliced garlic cloves in 4 tbsp olive oil. Add 2 tins San Marzano tomatoes crushed by hand and simmer 25 minutes. Cook 500g spaghetti, toss through the sauce with basil and 30g butter, and finish with grated parmesan.

w.note: his plant, which always gets the window
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate and cool slightly. Whisk in 3 yolks, then fold in 300ml whipped cream and 3 whites whipped to soft peaks. Layer in four small cups with 150g crushed chocolate biscuits as soil. Chill 3 hours and plant a mint sprig in each.
